types.Ref: words naming something in the scene (an item, a place, a part or control of an asset), resolved against what is there now; 'it' is the item in hand
types.Frac: fraction of a part's travel, 0 to 1 ('halfway', '25%', 'fully')
types.Level: a stop of a telescopic handle, 0 (retracted) to its top stop
types.Extent: number of detent clicks to turn a dial (positive = up)
types.Count: a positive whole number of repetitions
types.Spot: where in the case: a named spot, or the item centre in cm from the inside of the wheel-end wall (along) and from the hinge-side wall (across)
types.Angle: degrees about the vertical; 0 = the item's long side across the case
types.Orient: upright | lying (the bottle); flat for everything else
types.Style: half (folding in thirds is not simulated: see the fold verb)

steps: Resolve the place, or the item (then its current place).

Reachable in one step only if it is in the person's room, or in view: an unobstructed line from eye height (1.55 m) to it past walls, door frames and furniture. Otherwise the request is expanded: enter(room) for each room on the way until the target is in view, then look_at(item) for an item that has to be found, then go_to (each step logged with its parent). go_to(room) is the enters alone.
Stand point: a station's default spot, or in front of the item at the station's standoff.
Route: shortest path on the walking graph, shortcut wherever the straight line keeps 30 cm from furniture; a carried item is turned the way round that keeps it clear of walls.
Walk at the persona's speed and turn to face the station.
go_to.check: if carrying, the item is still between the hands (< 30 cm)

steps: Resolve the room; it must open off the person's room (a step of the walking graph crosses into it).
Entry point: the first walking-graph point inside that room on the way from here to its centre: fixed by the room and where the person stands, never an argument.
Walk there through the doorway (or across the open-plan boundary) at the persona's speed; a carried item is turned the way round that keeps it clear of walls.
enter.check: if carrying, the item is still between the hands (< 30 cm); the person ends inside the room
enter.effect: room := room (standing at its entry point)

steps: Resolve the reference to a point (item centre, part centre or station).
Turn the head (gaze target) towards it; the body does not move.
Cast a ray in the physics scene from eye height to it; anything static (walls, door frames, furniture) hit first means it is not in sight.
look_at.check: recorded: the target is in sight (look_check event)

steps: Resolve the item; it must be within reach (at this station, or in the open case with nothing on it).
Grasp by family: folded piles and boxes with a two-hand side squeeze across the short side, the bottle with a one-hand power wrap just above its centre of mass.
Targets from the item's observed pose: palms outside the faces, then in by 7-10 mm.
Lift 10-12 cm and test: the item must rise with the hands by contact alone.
Carry in front of the chest at max(1.0 m, start + 10 cm).
pick_up.check: item rose >= 70 % of the hand lift by contact (no attachment)

steps: The item must be the one in hand.
Destination: 'in' the case at a Spot (named or measured), 'on' another packed item, 'beside' one (on a given side), or on a station's surface.
Pose: Spot -> (x, y) in the case frame; yaw default puts the squeezed side along the case length; the bottle 'upright' or 'lying'.

Fit (5 mm height map of what is packed): inside the liner walls, resting on the highest surface under it with >= 60 % support, nothing fragile underneath, top below the closed lid, clear of the lid's swing, room for the hands beside the squeezed faces.
Lower to the measured top of the supports (live poses), open the grip along the palm normals, lift clear.
place.check: item rests within 7 cm of the requested centre inside the walls; bottle within 10 deg of vertical (upright) or > 70 deg (lying)
place.effect: item := in case at (x, y, yaw), on its supports

steps: The item must be the one in hand and the person at its home station.
Lower it to its starting pose on that surface and release.
put_back.check: item within 8 cm of where it started

steps: Resolve the part; check the asset supports 'open' on it and the value (the lid only fully, a zip to any fraction).
Lid: from the foot of the bed, hook the fingertips under the free edge's zip-track lip, swing it past its balance point (~64 deg) and let it fall open.
Zip: pinch the slider and run it back along the track to the requested fraction.
open.check: lid > 150 deg open; zip slider at the fraction

steps: Resolve the part and the value as for open.
Lid: hook the free edge, test-lift it, swing it over briskly past the balance point; if it slips the hook is released and tried again in a different place.
Zip: press the lid down with one palm, pinch the slider and run it along the track to the fraction; fully closed engages only after a closure check (lid < 2.5 deg).
close.check: lid < 3 deg; zip at the fraction

steps: Resolve the control (a button).
Fingertip to 1 cm above the button along its axis, then in until the measured contact force exceeds the button's spring (detected from contacts, not assumed).
Hold for `hold` seconds; release; repeat `times` times.
press.check: button travel reached its stop for >= hold
press.effect: device reacts (lock releases the zip pulls; the handle latch frees)

steps: Resolve the dial; exactly one of `to` / `by`.
Read the dial; the shorter way round gives the clicks to go.
Fingertip on the exposed rim, drag tangentially one detent at a time; re-read after each flick (closed loop) until the reading equals the target.
turn.check: dial reads the target digit (joint angle within half a detent)

steps: Resolve the control or device and parse the setting for it (Code for the lock, Level for the trolley handle).
Lock: turn each dial to its digit (as `turn`).
Trolley handle: grip the bar, press the button in the grip, pull or push to the stop, release the button so the latch engages.
set.check: lock dials read the code; handle latched within 5 mm of the stop

steps: Resolve the zip pulls; the zip must be fully closed.
Pinch both pulls and push them into the lock's slots until they latch.
Resolve the strap; the lid must be closed.
Pinch the male buckle, align it with the female and push until it clicks.
Resolve the strap.
Squeeze the two side-release tabs and pull the male half out.
The case must be closed and zipped; from the foot of the bed.
Two-hand overhand grip on the trolley bar (test pull, re-grip if it slips).
Tip it up onto its wheels with the wrists following the case, lift it off the bed, carry it past the bed end and set it down; release while rising.
stand_up.check: case within 10 deg of upright on four wheels

steps: Not simulated yet: requests are rejected (unsupported_operation).
The case must stand on its wheels with the trolley handle at a stop above 0.
Grip the handle, walk the route to the place pushing the case alongside on its 360-degree wheels (the way the manuals recommend), let go.
roll.check: case upright within 20 cm of the destination

steps: The loose towel lies flat on the kitchen counter, its near edge hanging over the counter's front edge.
Both flat hands, palms up, slide under the hanging edge (a third in from each corner), lift it, draw back past the counter's lip and rise above the towel.
Carry the edge over to just past the far edge, lower it, tip the fingertips down so it slides off them onto the towel, lift the hands away.
fold.check: the towel's depth shrank to 0.5 of flat (+-0.2), measured on the simulated cloth

steps: Not simulated: the folded edge lies flat on the towel, where neither the scoop nor a pinch can get under it with this hand model (the cloth is too coarse to bunch).
Arms at rest; hold for the duration.
Arms at rest; the utterance is logged as an event (question / plan-change channel).

macros.pack: go_to(item) -> pick_up(item) -> go_to(suitcase) -> place(item, in, suitcase, at)
macros.lock: close(main_zip) -> insert(zip_pulls, into=lock) -> turn dials away from the code

open.why: the lid only stays put closed or lying fully open

close.why: the lid only stays put closed or lying fully open

unzip the case all the way

excluded.lay the bottle down: the lying placement is not reliable with the scanned case yet
excluded.unfold the towel: neither the scoop nor a pinch gets under the folded edge with this hand model
excluded.fold in thirds: only folding in half is simulated
excluded.carry the case by its side handle: the handle has a grip but no skill yet
excluded.change the lock's combination: needs a pen in the reset hole; there is no pen in the scene
